claims.text: `auditing-mcp/SKILL.md` uses the severity vocabulary `BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR/NIT` (no INFO).
`review-architecture-auditor.md` and `review-cross-artifact-auditor.md` use the severity vocabulary `BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR/INFO` (no NIT).
`verdict_compute.py` is the canonical superset accepting both NIT and INFO as distinct values.
The bridge author preserves both NIT and INFO per ADR-0061's "document non-monotonic edges, don't collapse them" guidance.
Reviewer-discipline `critical` severity blocks acceptance, applies to architecturally wrong / security-breaking / contract violation / fundamentally infeasible findings, and cannot be deferred.
Reviewer-discipline `important` severity should be fixed before approval but isn't architecturally fatal, degrades the score, and is deferrable only with explicit user approval plus ledger entry.
Reviewer-discipline `recommended` severity is an improvement suggestion and is non-blocking.
Reviewer-discipline verdict mapping: any `critical` finding maps to needs_revision.
Reviewer-discipline verdict mapping: `important` only + consistency>80 + completeness>75 maps to approved_with_conditions.
Reviewer-discipline verdict mapping: only `recommended` + consistency>90 + completeness>85 maps to approved.
Reviewer-discipline verdict mapping: many critical findings maps to rejected.
The PV vocabulary is `blocking` / `warning` / `informational`, inlined in `test-phase-validator-author.md` Phase 2 and not in KB-task-decomposition (per parent Known Issue 3).

Non-monotonic edge NIT ↔ recommended: auditor side has -0.5 weight with "taste" framing; reviewer/PV side is non-blocking with "improvement" framing; NIT → recommended is safe, but the reverse loses actionability.

Non-monotonic edge MAJOR ↔ {blocking, warning}: auditor side has -5 weight with conditional_pass if no BLOCKER; reviewer/PV side depends on PV invariant blocking-class; default MAJOR → blocking, with downgrade to warning only with per-finding rationale.
Non-monotonic edge NIT vs INFO (intra-auditor): NIT is -0.5 in auditing-mcp; INFO is 0 in arch/cross auditors; the bridge preserves the distinction as NIT = taste/style, INFO = neutral observation.
